issues.title: Reconcile the post-refactor Luna gate audit into the canonical r2 work ledger
issues.body:
## Classification

- Type: Integration / testing-ledger reconciliation
- Desire: High
- Effort: Low
- Area: Integration / Testing
- Target: `release/0.1.0-r2`

## Observation / problem

The 2026-08-18 post-refactor Luna A/B/C/D audits show that the core r2 regression net survived, but gate promotion is not complete. The lane summaries disagree in detail because Luna D independently reclassified the 42-contract corpus and reports **10 MISSING** contracts, while some lane audit artifacts are currently only present in local worktrees/not inspectable from the remote branches.

A train worker must not need Coordinator chat history or access to another agent's local worktree to know what remains. Every actionable post-refactor finding must therefore be made durable in GitHub and mapped to exactly one canonical Issue/restoration owner.

This Issue owns **ledger reconciliation only**. It does not implement the Product/test gaps itself and must not become a duplicate umbrella implementation Issue.

## Current known mapping

At creation time, Coordinator reconciliation has identified:

- #93 — canonical Product Issue remains open; current r2 still uses `object-fit: cover`, and the packaged geometry gate is also missing.
- #110 — canonical open Issue owns the missing installed hidden-file toggle/reopen/reload persistence proof.
- #81 — canonical open Testing Issue owns the missing composed taskbar lifecycle regression; eligibility remains blocked by #72 acceptance.
- #175 — still RED and actively owned by PR #337.
- #66 browser acceptance — quarantined/restoration owner #320.
- #86 browser acceptance — quarantined/restoration owner #330.
- #63 browser acceptance — restoration owner #308.
- #118 browser acceptance — restoration owner #303.
- sibling Explorer/window-lifetime readiness — restoration owner #251.
- #124 saved-preview acceptance — restoration owner #304.
- #113 packaged Text parity protection — new dedicated backfill Issue #344 because #113 itself is already closed.
- #180 — canonical open Issue owns the missing installed denied-fullscreen Photos acceptance.
- #114 — canonical open Product Issue remains genuinely RED for Markdown formatter/command behavior.
- #100 — canonical open Integration Issue owns the missing dependency-metadata migration/verifier and remains externally blocked on native GitHub dependency mutation capability.
- #87 — canonical open Issue owns the unresolved migration/provenance acceptance decision and permanent migration/preservation coverage.
- #184 / #185 — existing Product Issues already own TaskManager and Show Desktop; they are not new gate-promotion Issues and are currently targeted r2-or-later rather than being invented by this audit.

This list is not allowed to silently substitute for the full Luna-D table; the complete 42-contract result must be reconciled once the new audit artifacts are remotely accessible.

## Scope

- Make the final Luna A/B/C/D post-refactor audit artifacts accessible from durable remote repository state or copy their complete actionable tables into GitHub comments if an artifact is intentionally not promoted.
- Reconcile Luna D's 42-contract master table against the current live r2 source, Issues, PRs, required CI inventory, and quarantine ledger.
- For every `MISSING`, `STILL RED`, or `QUARANTINED` entry, identify exactly one canonical open Issue that owns the remaining work.
- Create a new Issue only when no existing canonical owner exists; do not clone open Product/restoration Issues.
- For closed historical Product Issues whose implementation is accepted but regression protection is missing, use a bounded testing-backfill Issue (as with #344 for #113) instead of silently reopening architecture work.
- Correct any audit classification contradicted by current source. Example: #93 is not test-only while current r2 still has `object-fit: cover`.
- Record `SUPERSEDED` rationale where a historical RED packet should never be promoted.
- Ensure all newly created Issues contain explicit acceptance criteria and `/triage` metadata.
- Ensure workers can discover the remaining work from GitHub alone without needing Coordinator chat or local Luna worktrees.

## Out of scope

- Implementing Product fixes or browser tests from this Issue.
- Merging/rebasing Luna historical TDD branches wholesale.
- Treating historical `.red` files as production tests merely to reduce the missing count.
- Creating duplicate Issues when an existing canonical Issue already owns the exact acceptance gap.
- Removing quarantine without the dedicated restoration Issue's required proof.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The final A/B/C/D post-refactor audit artifacts are remotely inspectable or their complete actionable contents are durably reproduced in GitHub.
- [ ] All 42 Luna-D contracts are reconciled against the current `release/0.1.0-r2` graph rather than an old audit SHA only.
- [ ] Every `MISSING` contract maps to exactly one open canonical Issue, with a newly created Issue only when no existing owner exists.
- [ ] Every `STILL RED` Product contract maps to its canonical Product Issue and is not misclassified as test-only promotion work.
- [ ] Every `QUARANTINED` browser contract maps to its dedicated restoration Issue and remains executable debt in the canonical quarantine inventory.
- [ ] Every `SUPERSEDED` contract has a concrete rationale showing why it should not be promoted.
- [ ] Existing open Issues receive the post-refactor audit evidence needed for train workers to understand the remaining acceptance boundary.
- [ ] Any new Issues have explicit scope/out-of-scope, acceptance criteria, target, and `/triage` metadata.
- [ ] No Product/refactor implementation is duplicated solely because the historical Luna file was not merged verbatim.
- [ ] The final reconciliation comment/table can be used by `train.py`/workers without access to Coordinator conversation history or local agent worktrees.

## Verification

Spot-check at least one Desktop/FileManager, Shell/Windowing, Native Apps, metadata/integration, and quarantined-browser contract against live GitHub/source. Confirm that a worker following only the resulting GitHub ledger can reach the correct Issue and acceptance criteria.

## Relationships

- Source audits: Luna A/B/C/D post-refactor promotion audits.
- #344 is the first newly created orphaned backfill found by this reconciliation.
- #295 remains the canonical r2 flaky/quarantine ledger; this Issue must not replace it.

issues.title: Backfill packaged Text editor parity acceptance for #113
issues.body:
## Classification

- Type: Testing / acceptance backfill
- Desire: High
- Effort: Medium
- Area: Testing / Native Apps / Text / Monaco
- Target: `release/0.1.0-r2`
- Source contract: #113

## Observation / problem

The post-refactor Luna-C promotion audit against `release/0.1.0-r2` at `c047aa7391046dc28efc4d187f8871bb0de4afd2` found that #113's product implementation is present and deterministic lower-layer coverage exists, but the specific **packaged Text parity assertions were never promoted into a permanent browser acceptance**.

#113 was closed after PR #318 with successful packaged CI, but successful execution of the generic packaged suite is not the same as an executable assertion that the Text editor's requested parity affordances render and work. The current regression net should make those browser-visible contracts explicit so later Monaco/native-app refactors cannot silently remove them.

This Issue owns the missing acceptance protection only. It does not reopen #113 product architecture or duplicate #67/#89/#200 Monaco worker/runtime authority.

## Scope

Add the smallest truthful installed/package browser regression for the accepted #113 Text behavior, using the normal filesystem -> association/open -> Process/Windowing -> Text/Monaco path.

The acceptance should prove browser-visible behavior that deterministic tests cannot fully establish:

- document-aware `filename - Monaco Editor` identity is rendered through the real native window/process path;
- canonical language/plain-text status is visible for representative resources, including intentional JavaScript mapping where supported;
- line/cursor/status presentation is visible after real Monaco readiness;
- minimap/text-preview configuration is represented in the actual Monaco editor;
- discoverable command UI exposes the accepted high-value commands such as Find, Replace, and Go to Line and routes them through the real Text/Monaco command seam;
- browser health remains strict for unexpected Monaco/worker/security/runtime errors.

Prefer extending an existing canonical packaged editor journey when that keeps the test smaller and clearer; otherwise add one dedicated Text parity spec. Do not create a second Monaco readiness/worker authority.

## Out of scope

- Reimplementing #113 product behavior unless the acceptance proves a current Product regression.
- Replacing or duplicating #67 packaged Monaco worker/readiness acceptance.
- Changing #89 Program Files worker transport or #200 shared Monaco host architecture.
- Markdown formatter/command work (#114).
- Screenshot/pixel-perfect infrastructure.
- Sleeps, timeout inflation, retry-as-fix, or test-only Product hooks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Current installed Plasmon opens a Text resource through the normal filesystem/association/process/window path and reaches real Monaco readiness.
- [ ] The browser test asserts the accepted document-aware `filename - Monaco Editor` identity.
- [ ] The test asserts visible canonical language/status/cursor presentation and at least one intentional non-plain-text mapping such as JavaScript where supported.
- [ ] The test proves the accepted minimap/text-preview configuration is present in the real Monaco surface.
- [ ] The test proves the accepted discoverable Find, Replace, and Go to Line affordances are present and route through the real editor command seam without reimplementing Monaco commands in the test.
- [ ] Existing keyboard/editor behavior is not weakened to make the browser test pass.
- [ ] BrowserHealth remains strict; no new generic warning/error allowance is introduced.
- [ ] The acceptance is part of the normal required r2 packaged/Specialist inventory rather than a historical `.red` file or optional local-only test.
- [ ] The canonical test-inventory verifier recognizes the new/extended acceptance.
- [ ] Focused execution and required latest-head CI are green on the implementation head.
- [ ] If the new acceptance exposes a genuine current Product defect, that defect is routed to the appropriate canonical Product Issue rather than hidden by weakening the test.

## Verification

Run the focused packaged Text acceptance against the installed Neutron/Plasmon path with the repository's normal browser-health policy. The intended result is permanent browser regression coverage for #113's already-accepted product behavior.

## Relationships

- #113 owns the accepted Text parity behavior and remains historical Product authority.
- #67 owns packaged Monaco editor/worker acceptance.
- #89 owns Program Files Monaco worker packaging/transport.
- #200 owns the shared Monaco browser-runtime host.
- #114 owns unresolved Markdown formatter/editor-command behavior.

## Audit provenance

Luna-C post-refactor audit summary: `MISSING — #113 packaged Text parity assertions` on r2 SHA `c047aa7391046dc28efc4d187f8871bb0de4afd2`.

issues.title: [r2 CI] Repair and restore #86 diagnostic-selection acceptance
issues.body:
## Classification

- Owner: **SOL CI**
- Target: `release/0.1.0-r2`
- Canonical Product behavior: #86
- Source Product PR: #274
- Classification: quarantined browser acceptance / FileManager setup-readiness stability
- Ledger: #295
- Quarantine PR: #329

## Exact acceptance

- Spec: `test/e2e/plasmon-diagnostic-selection-86.spec.ts`
- Test: `#86 diagnostic text selects without stealing FileEntry drag`

This Issue owns the acceptance's CI stability and restoration lifecycle. It does not replace Product Issue #86 and does not authorize rollback or Product behavior changes without deterministic Product-defect evidence.

## Unrelated Red-Gate evidence

PR #328 did not own #86 or the FileManager Product behavior introduced by #274, but its fresh Flake Probe run `31976275024` failed all ten matrix jobs at `Run fresh Plasmon probe`.

Attempt 1 / job `95236169034` archived the exact Specialist failure:

```text
[chromium] › test/e2e/plasmon-diagnostic-selection-86.spec.ts:9:1
#86 diagnostic text selects without stealing FileEntry drag

Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed
Locator: ... getByRole('textbox', { name: /^Rename New Folder(?: \(\d+\))?$/ }).last()
Expected: visible
Timeout: 20000ms
Error: element(s) not found

73 | await (await openFileManagerMenu()).getByRole("menuitem", { name: "New Folder" }).click();
74 | const folderRename = ...
75 | await expect(folderRename).toBeVisible();
```

Specialist result for the archived attempt: **1 failed / 8 passed**.

The failure occurs during setup/readiness after invoking `New Folder`, before the acceptance reaches the #86 diagnostic text-selection and post-diagnostic drag assertions. It therefore should not be attributed to unrelated PR #328, and this evidence alone does not prove the #274 Product behavior is wrong.

## Authorized temporary quarantine

Quarantine **only this exact test** with `@r2-quarantine`, linked to #86 and this Issue. Keep `test/e2e/plasmon-diagnostic-selection-86.spec.ts` in the Specialist inventory; normal Specialist/flake-probe execution should filter the tagged acceptance rather than delete the spec, broaden a skip, enable retries, or weaken the gate.

Do not quarantine other FileManager, diagnostic, drag, context-menu, or Explorer coverage.

## Repair / investigation requirements

Determine why the setup path can invoke `New Folder` without the expected rename textbox becoming visible. Investigate the real browser/readiness boundary first, including:

- context-menu target/action delivery;
- FileManager create-folder completion;
- rename/editor mount timing and state transition;
- projection/render refresh after the preceding `New Text Document` creation;
- whether the acceptance relies on an unstable browser interaction rather than a deterministic readiness signal.

Do not use as the repair:

- Playwright retries;
- sleeps;
- timeout inflation;
- weakened/fallback assertions;
- broad spec quarantine;
- Product-only test hooks.

If deterministic evidence proves a Product defect in #86/#274 behavior, route that Product correction separately rather than silently changing Product behavior from SOL CI.

## Restoration proof / exit criteria

Remove this acceptance's `@r2-quarantine` only after:

- the exact acceptance is exercised **unquarantined** with retries=0;
- the setup/readiness root cause is repaired or deterministically classified;
- five consecutive clean first-attempt packaged Specialist executions pass, or a stricter Coordinator-specified proof;
- the original #86 contracts remain intact: diagnostic text is selectable, entry drag state is not stolen, and post-dismissal FileEntry drag still works;
- no unrelated r2 quarantine, assertion, or required CI gate is weakened;
- `QUARANTINED_BROWSER_TESTS.md`, executable inventory verification, and ledger #295 are updated with restoration evidence.

Close this Issue only after the quarantine is removed and the restoration evidence is recorded.

issues.body:
Agent: SOL CI
Target: `release/0.1.0-r2`
Classification: **INVESTIGATION TASK** — shared CI/harness vs acceptance-owned flake not yet resolved
Ledger: #295

Two fresh flake-probe runs each completed 9/10 attempts successfully and failed one attempt:

- run `31923225478`, failed job `95106500771` — 9/10 pass; failed attempt 7/10
- run `31923958308`, failed job `95108418079` — 9/10 pass; failed attempt 3/10

Observed failure evidence includes the runtime signature:

`Too many concurrent frontend tool calls`

The failure occurred in the broad packaged/golden-path surface. Current evidence is sufficient to treat the behavior as intermittent, but not sufficient to assign it to one narrow test-owned acceptance.

## Investigation questions

- Do both failed jobs reduce to the same exact runtime/tool-call concurrency signature?
- Which process/test boundary is creating overlapping frontend tool calls?
- Is the concurrency exhaustion caused by shared Playwright/browser harness lifecycle, Product code, or one isolated acceptance?

1. a narrow acceptance-owned flake is identified, with an exact quarantine/restoration plan;

issues.title: [r2 CI] BrowserHealth Chromium sandbox-warning contamination
issues.body:
Agent: SOL CI
Target: `release/0.1.0-r2`

- `test/e2e/plasmon-drag-preview-66.spec.ts`
- `#66 active multi-selection drag preview is above windows and transparent to hit testing`

BrowserHealth rejects repeated Chromium console warnings emitted by the installed Kernel bundle:

`An iframe which has both allow-scripts and allow-same-origin for its sandbox attribute can escape its sandboxing.`

The known evidence contained two occurrences from the installed Kernel `chunks/main-LGUTTLHZ.js`, causing the final shared health assertion to fail even though the #66 interaction boundary completed.

- Packaged Browser run `31895316957`
- Specialist job `95037635705`
- first attempt: **FAIL**
- Playwright retry: **FAIL** with the same warning contamination
- PocketIC/environment: healthy
- product boundary: reached; #66 interaction completed before BrowserHealth failure

## Suspected ownership

Shared Kernel/browser-health boundary. SOL CI owns classification/reproduction; route Product/Kernel source changes only if exact evidence establishes the warning is a real security/product defect rather than a known browser diagnostic emitted by an intended sandbox configuration.

## Quarantine location

**None at test level. Deliberately not safe to quarantine by skipping #66.** The warning is shared BrowserHealth/session evidence and could surface in another acceptance. Skipping one product test would hide coverage without removing the underlying shared signature.

A quarantine change is permitted only if it can match this exact diagnostic at the shared health boundary without suppressing other console warnings/errors, and only after review proves doing so does not weaken a real security invariant.

- reproduce the exact warning with current r2 packaged Kernel/Plasmon and healthy PocketIC;
- identify the emitting iframe/sandbox contract and whether the warning is expected or actionable;
- if expected, implement an exact-message/source-bounded health classification rather than a generic warning ignore;
- if actionable, route the Product/Kernel repair to its authority owner;
- validate required Browser CI with no unrelated warnings hidden.

## Acceptance / quarantine removal criterion

No test-level quarantine exists to remove. This Issue is complete only when either (a) the warning no longer occurs in repeated healthy packaged runs, or (b) an explicitly reviewed exact-signature health rule classifies only this known diagnostic while every unknown console warning/error continues to fail CI. Record repeated clean evidence before closing.

issues.title: Add label-triggered fresh-run flake probe for r2 browser acceptance
issues.body:
## Classification

- Type: CI / flaky-test detection
- Desire: High
- Effort: Medium
- Area: Testing / Integration / Packaged Browser CI
- Target: `release/0.1.0-r2`

## Problem

The r2 train currently needs manual GitHub Actions reruns to establish whether a suspected browser acceptance test is genuinely stable. Existing required Playwright gates correctly fail on retry-classified flakes, but they do not provide a bounded, repeatable way to proactively probe a PR head for intermittent failures.

## Required capability

Introduce an opt-in PR label:

`ci:flake-probe`

When that label is present on a pull request, CI must run a dedicated diagnostic flake-probe workflow against the PR's current exact head. A subsequent `synchronize` event while the label remains present must probe the new exact head again.

The probe is diagnostic and MUST NOT replace or weaken the five required r2 release gates.

## Fresh-run invariant

Run 10 independent attempts using a GitHub Actions matrix so each attempt receives a fresh hosted runner and fresh package/PocketIC environment.

For each attempt:

- checkout the PR merge/head context used by GitHub Actions;
- use the normal Nix environment;
- package/provision through the same real demo path used by Specialist CI;
- run Playwright with `--workers=1` and **retries disabled for the probe**;
- preserve all product assertions, BrowserHealth checks, sandbox/security checks, and runtime readiness predicates;
- upload useful failure diagnostics where available.

A failed attempt is evidence. Do not retry an individual probe attempt to turn it green.

## Scope for first implementation

For label-triggered execution, probe the complete current r2 Specialist inventory rather than inventing changed-file relevance logic. This keeps the first version truthful and compatible with stacked PRs.

Also support manual `workflow_dispatch` so CI can later target a narrower known acceptance boundary without closing/reopening PRs.

## Summary semantics

The workflow should make the aggregate result obvious:

- `10/10` -> stability observed on this exact head;
- `<10/10` -> intermittent/deterministic failure observed;
- infrastructure/setup failures remain visible and are classified separately by the CI owner rather than hidden.

The workflow should surface the exact SHA being probed and the attempt number in logs/job names.

## Required safety boundaries

- Do not modify normal required-gate semantics from #226.
- Do not alter the r2 five-gate ruleset contract from #227.
- Do not add sleeps, retries, timeout inflation, weakened assertions, or test-only product hooks merely to improve the probe score.
- Do not use PR close/reopen as a trigger mechanism.
- Do not create changed-path/cheap-green logic in required workflows.
- Keep this workflow diagnostic unless a separate Coordinator decision makes it merge-required.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Adding `ci:flake-probe` to an r2 PR starts a dedicated probe.
- [ ] Ten fresh independent attempts run for the exact PR head/merge context.
- [ ] Probe Playwright retries are 0 and workers are 1.
- [ ] Each attempt uses real package/provision/runtime setup.
- [ ] Any failed attempt remains failed; no attempt-level retry masks it.
- [ ] Pushing a new commit while the label remains causes a new exact-head probe.
- [ ] Removing the label stops future automatic probes.
- [ ] `workflow_dispatch` exists for explicit/manual probing.
- [ ] Aggregate result clearly reports pass count out of 10.
- [ ] Existing required r2 workflows and branch/ruleset semantics are unchanged.
- [ ] CI documentation records the diagnostic/non-required ownership boundary.

## Ownership

SOL CI owns implementation, validation, failure classification, and future refinement. SOL 1 / SOL 2 product agents must not absorb probe failures into product code unless exact evidence identifies product ownership.

issues.title: Make required r2 Playwright gates fail when any test attempt is flaky
issues.body:
## Classification

- Type: Bug / CI gate correctness
- Desire: Critical
- Effort: Medium
- Area: Testing / Integration / Packaged Browser CI
- Target: `release/0.1.0-r2`

## Observation / problem

Required r2 Playwright/browser workflows currently permit CI retries. A test that fails its first attempt but passes on retry is classified by Playwright as flaky, the Playwright command exits 0, and GitHub therefore records the required workflow as successful.

This creates a release-gate escape: a real defect can be detected by BrowserHealth on an initial attempt and still enter the release because the retry passes.

## Proven RCA

Historical evidence from completed #217 established this exact sequence:

1. Packaged Smoke detected a real first-party `folder.svg -> net::ERR_ABORTED` BrowserHealth failure.
2. CI Playwright retried the failed test.
3. The retry passed.
4. Playwright classified the test as flaky rather than failed.
5. The command exited 0.
6. GitHub therefore reported the required check green.
7. The merge gate enforced the final successful check conclusion, not the fact that an earlier test attempt failed.

#217 is complete and must not be reopened or modified by this Issue.

## Required invariant

A required r2 release-gating Playwright workflow MUST NOT report green if any test failed an attempt.

Retries may remain for diagnostics, traces, and distinguishing intermittent from deterministic failures, but gate semantics are:

```text
passed first attempt
-> GREEN

failed then passed retry
-> RED / nonzero

failed all attempts
-> RED / nonzero
```

## Scope

- Inspect every required r2 Playwright/browser workflow that consumes the shared Playwright configuration.
- Implement the smallest correct hardening that makes flaky Playwright results fail required release-gating lanes.
- Preserve useful retry diagnostics unless there is a concrete reason not to.
- Do not weaken BrowserHealth, package validation, test assertions, security/runtime failure detection, or required browser coverage.
- Add regression/CI proof that a deliberately flaky test which fails once and passes on retry causes the relevant command to exit nonzero.
- Verify whether GitHub branch protection/rulesets actually enforce the intended required r2 checks, and report any merge-enforcement configuration gap separately from Playwright exit semantics.
- Update durable testing/CI documentation only where the release-gate invariant needs to be recorded for future maintainers.

## Out of scope

- Reopening or changing #217.
- Removing retries merely to hide the distinction between flaky and deterministic failures without a concrete reason.
- Unrelated CI cleanup.
- Sol 1 or Sol 2 product work.
- Weakening or allowlisting BrowserHealth failures.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Every required r2 release-gating Playwright/browser lane exits nonzero if any test failed an attempt, even if a retry passes.
- [x] A first-attempt pass remains green.
- [x] A test that exhausts retries remains red.
- [x] Useful retry diagnostics/traces remain available unless explicitly justified otherwise.
- [x] Regression/CI proof demonstrates the fail-then-pass case exits nonzero.
- [x] BrowserHealth and package/test failure detection remain strict and unchanged unless strengthening is required.
- [x] Required r2 browser workflows using the shared Playwright configuration are enumerated and verified.
- [x] GitHub ruleset/branch-protection enforcement is checked independently; any enforcement gap is reported precisely.
- [x] Exact-head required CI is green for the hardening implementation itself before Ready.

## Verification

Use a deterministic deliberately-flaky fixture/test or equivalent bounded proof to establish exit-code semantics without making production browser tests genuinely flaky. Validate the required r2 Playwright workflows on the exact PR head.

- Historical escape evidence: #217 (complete; do not reopen/modify).
- Related testing infrastructure: #33, #167, #187.
- Related required-check reporting semantics: #143.

issues.title: Establish r2 refactor-guard smoke suite for Plasmon production boundaries
issues.body:
## Classification

- Type: Task
- Desire: High
- Effort: High
- Area: Testing / Integration
- Target: `release/0.1.0-r2`
- Public Plasmon version remains `0.1.0`

## Objective

Establish a small, refactor-oriented smoke suite that protects Plasmon's observable architectural contracts and common assembled workflows without freezing React structure, source layout, private state, CSS implementation, or intermediary call graphs.

A substantial internal refactor should remain free to move modules/components/services, but CI must fail quickly if production composition, canonical resource opening, filesystem identity, Process/Windowing/Shell convergence, Start/Search projections, `.sys` / `.neutron` authority, persistence reconstruction, packaged runtime health, or critical geometry stops working.

Build on the shared testing foundation established by #167. Keep `createHeadlessPlasmonEnvironment()` authoritative for deterministic composition and `renderPlasmon()` as the bounded RTL adapter. Use the manifest-driven installed demo environment for real package/browser boundaries.

## Core design rule

Test observable subsystem-boundary contracts, not source structure.

Prefer invariants such as canonical resource existence/identity, one logical activation, correct owning authority, durable identity through mutation/recomposition, projection uniqueness, service-authoritative presentation, and clean browser/runtime health.

Avoid exact component hierarchy, private state shape, internal function naming, CSS class assertions where semantic access exists, or exact intermediary-call counts unless cardinality is itself architectural.

## Scope

### Fast deterministic / production-composition guards

Add compact cross-system smoke coverage for:

1. boot / assembled-system health;
2. canonical filesystem/resource -> association -> OpenService -> native handler / runtime / NeutronBridge routing;
3. representative native `.sys` and installed `.neutron` source-of-truth behavior;
4. filesystem NodeId lifecycle across create -> rename -> move -> open -> Trash -> restore;
5. application activation -> Process -> Windowing -> taskbar convergence, including two simultaneous native windows when cheap;
6. Start/Search projecting authoritative native app, Neutron app, and ordinary file resources rather than maintaining independent catalogs;
7. Desktop/FileManager observing and activating the same authoritative resource, including one shortcut;
8. persistence/reconstruction across two independent production compositions sharing one repository.

Reuse existing focused tests where they already prove lower-level semantics. This Issue owns representative refactor guards and shared composition, not feature-specific exhaustive coverage.

### Bounded RTL guards

Use `renderPlasmon()` for only the React/DOM adapter claims needed to prove assembled common paths remain wired after a UI rewrite. Prefer semantic roles/names/user actions and avoid a Page Object Model.

Representative coverage should include boot-visible Shell surfaces plus a small Process/Windowing/taskbar and Start/Search/Desktop/FileManager interaction path that still delegates to production authorities.

### Shared packaged/browser health

Create one shared Playwright/browser-health fixture/helper used by the refactor smoke and reusable by existing packaged specs where practical.

Default policy: unexpected `pageerror`, uncaught/unhandled browser error observable to Playwright, `console.error`, `console.warn`, failed first-party requests, Plasmon-owned 404/5xx assets, required worker startup failure, or browser security error associated with required Plasmon functionality fails the test. Keep any allowlist explicit and very small.

Add a small packaged common-path smoke using the manifest-driven #167 environment that proves real boot, core first-party assets, one native app/document path, Monaco worker initialization, Review `.neutron`, and one representative runtime-handled resource without duplicating every specialist browser suite.

### Geometry sanity

Add tolerant gross-geometry assertions for representative Desktop rename, default-opened window reachability, Search popup/control containment, and taskbar menu viewport anchoring. Do not encode pixel-perfect styling.

### Visual-regression feasibility spike

Evaluate 3-5 stable states with focused/region Playwright screenshots. Document CI/font/rendering stability, expected diff/update workflow, baseline ownership, and whether any visual snapshots should become a required r2 gate. Do not create a broad golden-image system unless evidence supports it.

### Durable refactor contract inventory

Add a concise table/document mapping boundary -> authority -> consumer -> smoke, so refactor authors can see which externally observable contracts must survive subsystem replacement.

### CI organization

Keep lanes tiered:

- Fast PR smoke: deterministic/headless + bounded RTL refactor guards on Plasmon-relevant PRs.
- Packaged Browser Smoke: small real installed/package/runtime common path on relevant paths using the #167 manifest-driven environment.
- Full acceptance: specialist slower browser/runtime/emulator/persistence/visual work remains separate.

Do not create one enormous slow workflow or make every Plasmon PR wait for every expensive emulator/game scenario.

## Highest-value regressions to catch

The suite should fail if a refactor accidentally:

- replaces stable NodeId semantics with paths;
- creates a second native-app catalog;
- treats `/Apps/*.neutron` as install authority;
- bypasses AssociationRegistry/OpenService;
- gives Desktop/FileManager independent launch policy;
- makes application = window;
- makes Shell own Process state;
- moves window authority into React;
- creates fake `.sys` wrappers for runtimes;
- duplicates filesystem policy in UI components;
- silently swallows bootstrap/reconciliation errors;
- moves durable state into localStorage;
- breaks required package/runtime/worker paths;
- creates duplicate managed resources during reconstruction.

## Product-defect handling

If a valid smoke exposes a current product defect, preserve the RED evidence, identify or create the smallest canonical product Issue, and hand it off. Do not silently fix product behavior in this testing Issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] One strict deterministic assembled-boot smoke proves core authorities/resources/projections are alive and unique.
- [x] Representative canonical open smoke covers native text, Markdown, Review `.neutron`, and one runtime-handled resource without surface-specific launch policy.
- [x] Representative `.sys` / `.neutron` authority and projection uniqueness are guarded.
- [x] Compact NodeId lifecycle smoke composes create/rename/move/open/Trash/restore through production authorities.
- [x] Process/Windowing/taskbar convergence is guarded without Shell owning parallel runtime state.
- [x] Start/Search projection smoke covers native app, Neutron app, and ordinary document through canonical activation.
- [x] Desktop/FileManager shared-resource + shortcut smoke proves shared filesystem/open authority.
- [x] Persistence/reconstruction smoke reuses one repository across two independent production compositions and detects duplicate managed resources.
- [x] Shared packaged-browser health helper fails unexpected browser/runtime warnings/errors/failed first-party requests with only explicit minimal allowlisting.
- [x] Small packaged refactor smoke proves real boot, required first-party assets/workers, Review, and representative runtime path using the #167 environment.
- [x] Tolerant gross-geometry sanity coverage exists without freezing styling.
- [x] Bounded visual-regression spike is completed and recommendation documented.
- [x] Durable refactor contract inventory is checked in.
- [x] CI tiers clearly separate fast refactor smoke, packaged browser smoke, and slower full acceptance.
- [x] No product behavior redesign or weakened security/package validation.
- [x] Required latest-head CI is green before Ready handoff.

## Relationships / exclusions

- Builds on merged #167 and its canonical headless/RTL/manifest-driven browser harness.
- Does not replace focused subsystem tests.
- Does not replace the separate real-browser persistence investigation (#186).
- Does not absorb unrelated r1/r2 product defects.
- Does not build a giant Page Object Model or full-desktop screenshot gate by default.

issues.title: Establish the r2 shared RTL harness and representative integration test layer
issues.body:
## Classification

- Type: Task
- Desire: High
- Effort: High
- Area: Testing / Integration

The r2 TDD staging ledger at `planning/release-0.1.0-r2-tdd/apps/plasmon/test/tdd/todo.md` explicitly routes shared harness/CI gaps to Testing / Integration rather than asking Luna spec agents or domain implementors to invent test infrastructure.

## Expected / desired outcome

Establish one canonical r2 testing system that composes the existing real production authorities, extends the #30 headless environment where necessary, adds a small React Testing Library + `@testing-library/user-event` + Happy DOM adapter layer, and keeps Playwright limited to genuinely browser/package-owned evidence.

Domain implementors should be able to consume shared helpers and red gates without designing a second fake Plasmon implementation or a large Page Object Model.

## Architecture / authority constraints

- Preserve and extend `createHeadlessPlasmonEnvironment`; do not replace it with RTL.
- `PlasmonOS` should be rendered with the same real production `PlasmonServices` graph wherever possible.
- Fake only true external boundaries already owned by the test harness, such as persistence snapshots, Neutron listing/runtime adapters, deterministic viewport/window record adapters, or browser/package facilities.
- Prefer `renderPlasmon()`, `screen.getByRole(...)`, and `userEvent...`; add Plasmon-specific semantic helpers only after repeated use proves value.
- Prefer accessible role/name/state queries. `data-testid` is a last resort for stable semantic roles not expressible accessibly.
- Do not move filesystem, association/opening, Process, Windowing, Shell, Desktop, native-app, or game semantics into test helpers.
- Narrow production testability refactors are allowed only when existing deterministic behavior is trapped in React; extract that behavior into the proper production controller/model/command, preserve behavior, and add focused regression coverage.
- Do not implement new feature/domain semantics in this Issue merely to make a test pass.

## HARNESS GAP policy

Classify Luna/runtime requests as:

A. existing production seam already usable;
B. missing test adapter/helper;
C. missing React/RTL harness capability;
D. existing deterministic production behavior trapped in React and requiring narrow extraction;
E. genuine browser boundary requiring minimal Playwright.

Testing / Integration owns A-D repairs where appropriate. E must be documented explicitly and kept minimal in Playwright.

## Scope

### 1. Canonical Bun/headless composition

Keep the existing #30 environment authoritative and add only reusable builders/fixtures/inspection seams that are required by representative r2 workflows.

Establish or consolidate representative system coverage for at least:

- Desktop selection/activation/context commands;
- rename;
- shortcuts;
- FileManager navigation;
- copy/cut/paste;
- Trash lifecycle;
- Start;
- Search;
- taskbar/process/window lifecycle;
- filesystem/open/association dispatch;
- persistence/recomposition;
- managed filesystem bootstrap;
- Neutron application projections;
- Text/Markdown deterministic document lifecycle;
- js-dos/EmulatorJS deterministic runtime selection.

Reuse existing focused tests/issues rather than duplicating them; this Issue owns shared composition and representative cross-system coverage, not feature semantics.

### 2. Bounded RTL middle layer

Add the minimum test dependencies/setup required for Bun + React Testing Library + `@testing-library/user-event` + Happy DOM.

Provide a reusable `renderPlasmon()`-style test root that:

- injects a real production-backed Plasmon service graph;
- performs deterministic setup/cleanup;
- exposes only small semantic helpers/builders that have demonstrated reuse;
- does not become a Page Object Model or parallel UI implementation.

Add representative adapter coverage for:

- Desktop click/double-click/right-click;
- context-menu command activation;
- rename keyboard flow;
- Start open/dismiss;
- Search entry/activation;
- taskbar interaction;
- dialog/menu interaction.

### 3. Playwright boundary cleanup

Keep packaged/browser tests only where the browser/package owns the behavior, including real geometry/layout/hit-testing, pointer capture/stacking/focus where DOM simulation is insufficient, iframe/sandbox behavior, workers, Monaco real initialization, emulator/canvas runtime, media codecs, fullscreen/download/file-picker, and final installed-package HTTP/runtime boundaries.

Where deterministic golden-path assertions are already covered by the new Bun/headless/RTL layers, stop broadly duplicating those semantics in Playwright. Preserve the smallest real browser/package proof needed for integration confidence.

### 4. Test lanes and TDD consumption

- Organize deterministic/headless, RTL adapter, and packaged/browser boundaries into clear canonical commands/CI lanes without weakening required gates.
- Provide the smallest shared red-gate/helper conventions needed by the r2 TDD staging ledger.
- Keep CI scope decisions centralized in Testing / Integration rather than copied into Luna/domain PRs.
- Required checks must report; irrelevant expensive work should cheap-skip successfully rather than disappear.

### 5. Durable documentation

- New Desktop, Shell, Windowing, Native Apps, Games, filesystem, association, or process feature semantics.
- A second fake Plasmon OS/service implementation.
- A giant Page Object Model.
- Broad UI redesign or accessibility redesign unrelated to establishing stable semantic test access.
- Replacing legitimate packaged/browser evidence with simulated DOM tests.
- Wholesale merge of the intentionally-red r2 TDD planning branch.

issues.title: Migrate Issue-to-Issue sequencing from blocked labels to native GitHub dependencies
issues.body:
## Observation / problem

Plasmon's workflow prefers native GitHub Issue dependencies (`blocked by` / `blocking`) for real engineering sequencing, but the current connector cannot mutate those relationships. During rapid backlog creation, several dependent Issues therefore use a `blocked` label plus prose in `## Dependencies / relationships` as a temporary approximation.

The backlog is now large enough that leaving Issue-to-Issue dependencies encoded only as labels/prose makes eligibility harder for agents/reviewers to query and conflates normal dependency sequencing with exceptional external blockers.

## Expected / desired outcome

Audit the current open Plasmon Issues and represent genuine Issue-to-Issue sequencing using GitHub's native dependency graph. Reserve the generic `blocked` label for exceptional/external blockers or unresolved decisions that cannot be represented as an Issue dependency.

## Evidence / reproduction

Additional open Issues may have been created since this list and must be audited live rather than assuming this snapshot is exhaustive.

## Context and architecture constraints

- GitHub Issues remain the canonical work/dependency source of truth.
- Native dependencies represent actual sequencing only; do not connect Issues merely because they are related.
- Preserve `blocked` for external capability/security/decision blockers where there is no canonical predecessor Issue.
- Do not create fake dependency Issues solely to eliminate a label.
- Do not change implementation scope, priority, acceptance criteria, or ownership while migrating metadata.
- Use the live Issue bodies/current state as authority and skip already-closed/superseded dependencies appropriately.

## Scope

- Audit all open Issues carrying `blocked` and all open Issues whose dependency section says `blocked by`/equivalent.
- For each true Issue-to-Issue prerequisite, add native GitHub dependency relationship(s).
- Verify dependency direction carefully (`dependent` is blocked by `prerequisite`).
- Remove the generic `blocked` label when the only blocker is fully represented by native Issue dependencies and no external blocker remains.
- Retain `blocked` when an external/non-Issue blocker remains and document that blocker clearly.
- Correct stale dependency prose if the live predecessor already merged/closed and no longer blocks implementation.
- Spot-check agent queue eligibility after migration.
- Update workflow docs only if needed to clarify native dependency vs exceptional-label usage.

## Out of scope

- Parent/sub-issue hierarchy redesign for every backlog item.
- Reprioritizing Issues.
- Changing Area/Desire/Effort metadata.
- Closing dependent Issues.
- Automatically beginning implementation when a dependency clears.
- Writing a generic GitHub project-management service unless repeated manual migration demonstrates a real need.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every currently open Issue-to-Issue sequencing blocker discovered in the audit is represented with the correct native GitHub dependency direction.
- [ ] Generic `blocked` labels are removed where native Issue dependencies fully represent the blocker and no external blocker remains.
- [ ] External/decision/security blockers retain an appropriate exceptional-state label and clear explanation.
- [ ] Closed/merged prerequisites do not leave dependents falsely blocked.
- [ ] No merely-related Issues are incorrectly made prerequisites.
- [ ] Agent queue eligibility can be determined from native dependency state plus exceptional labels without parsing chat history.
- [ ] Workflow documentation remains accurate about dependency vs blocked-label semantics.

## Verification

issues.title: Stop showing the technical search safety-limit warning for ordinary result truncation
issues.body:
## Observation / problem

Shell Search uses one `truncated` flag for two different conditions: filesystem traversal hitting its safety node limit and ordinary per-category/result caps intentionally trimming otherwise valid matches. The visible Shell renders the same technical warning whenever `truncated` is true:

`Search reached its local safety/result limit; refine the query for more matches.`

That means a normal query with more than the configured category cap can show a warning that sounds like search encountered an abnormal safety limit even though the product merely applied its normal presentation cap.

## Expected / desired outcome

Separate abnormal/incomplete filesystem-search truncation from ordinary result-list capping so users only see a warning when search is genuinely incomplete because a safety/error boundary was reached. Ordinary result caps should have normal, non-alarming presentation.

## Evidence / reproduction

`applyResultLimits()` sets `truncated = true` whenever a category contains more results than its configured limit or total output exceeds `SEARCH_TOTAL_LIMIT`. `searchShell()` ORs that value with filesystem traversal truncation. `Shell.tsx` then renders the technical safety-limit warning for any `searchBatch.truncated` result.

## Context and architecture constraints

- Keep bounded search limits for performance/safety.
- Do not remove traversal safety guards or silently pretend an actually incomplete filesystem scan is complete.
- Shell owns presentation; Search model should expose enough structured reason/state for truthful UI.
- Do not introduce a search database/index as part of this Issue.
- Deterministic distinction belongs in headless/model tests, not Playwright.

## Scope

- Distinguish ordinary result-cap trimming from traversal/safety truncation in the Search result model.
- Preserve existing category/total caps unless evidence supports a separate tuning Issue.
- Show a technical/incomplete-search warning only when the filesystem scan genuinely stops because of a safety/incomplete boundary or recorded search warning condition.
- For ordinary capped results, either remain silent or expose a normal `more results`/refine affordance consistent with current Shell UX without alarming wording.
- Add focused tests covering category cap, total cap, max-node traversal truncation, and warning rendering decisions.
- Keep search cancellation/latest-result behavior unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Search indexing/catalog redesign.
- Raising limits simply to hide the warning.
- Search result classification (#49).
- Visual redesign of the Search panel.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Exceeding a normal category/result presentation cap does not produce the technical local-safety warning.
- [x] Hitting the filesystem traversal safety boundary remains detectable and produces truthful incomplete-search feedback.
- [x] Existing result caps remain enforced unless deliberately changed with evidence.
- [x] Search model exposes structured enough state that Shell does not infer safety failure from ordinary capping.
- [x] Focused tests cover ordinary cap vs actual traversal truncation.
- [x] No Playwright coverage is required for this deterministic distinction.
- [x] `npm --workspace neutron-plasmon test` passes on the current PR head.
- [x] Shell Search documentation remains accurate.

## Verification

Use deterministic Search model/controller tests plus the full Plasmon fast lane. A packaged/manual glance may confirm final wording, but browser automation is not needed for the semantic distinction.

## Dependencies / relationships

Independent Shell Search correctness issue. If #32 is still in flight, implement after it merges to avoid unnecessary overlap in Shell files; base advancement alone is not a reason to merge parent into an unrelated active branch.

## Cross-domain review

- Testing: only if shared Search test helpers change.

issues.title: Exclude runtime-only native hosts such as js-dos from Start application seeding
issues.body:
## Observation / problem

As a result, a runtime-only host can be seeded into Start like a first-class application even though its own source explicitly states that it is not a filesystem `.sys` application and should be reached by opening a `.jsdos` resource.

## Expected / desired outcome

Separate user-launchable native application inventory from runtime-only process-host registration so association-driven runtimes such as js-dos do not appear in Start merely because Process needs a host definition.

## Evidence / reproduction

`registerWave2Applications()` registers `jsDosRuntimeDefinition` into `NativeApplicationRegistry` and comments that this exists only because current OpenService routes local React hosts through `NativeProcessController`. `startMenu.ts::desiredSeeds()` currently maps all `nativeApps` into Start shortcuts without distinguishing runtime-only hosts.

- js-dos remains a normal association/runtime handler selected by `.jsdos` resources.
- Do not create `DOS.sys`, `Games.sys`, or another fake application wrapper.
- Process host registration and user-launchable app catalog semantics are distinct even if they currently share `NativeAppDefinition` storage.
- Avoid inventing a broad `ApplicationCatalog` framework; add the smallest durable metadata/projection seam that solves the demonstrated distinction.
- Preserve legitimate first-class native apps such as Explorer, Settings, Text, Markdown, Photos, Video, Browser, Properties, Recycle Bin, etc.

## Scope

- Define the smallest explicit way to mark/expose a native process host as runtime-only/non-Start-launchable.
- Ensure js-dos uses that classification without changing association or process-host behavior.
- Make Start reconciliation seed only legitimate user-launchable native applications.
- Ensure runtime-only definitions do not leak into other app-only Shell surfaces merely because they are registered with Process; audit Start and direct native-app search projection in the same bounded change.
