## Observation / problem

Shell taskbar behavior depends on live Process and Windowing state, but most taskbar semantics are currently proven through isolated model tests. Issue #72 improves the taskbar presentation model for pinned/running/active/launching state, yet a cross-authority regression is still needed to prove real process/window transitions produce the expected Shell taskbar projection.

## Expected / desired outcome

Use the shared headless Plasmon environment to prove the taskbar reacts coherently to production Process and Windowing lifecycle transitions without moving lifecycle authority into Shell or requiring Playwright for deterministic state.

## Evidence / reproduction

The current Shell model derives native taskbar entries from pinned preferences plus live process records and computes focus/minimize actions from Windowing state. The testing protocol explicitly identifies taskbar/process/window derivation as a good headless seam.

## Context and architecture constraints

- Process remains authoritative for native process lifecycle.
- Windowing remains authoritative for focus/minimize/restore state.
- Shell owns only the taskbar projection and user action dispatch.
- Do not invent Shell-owned shadow running/focused state.
- Do not re-test visual styling or DOM-only details headlessly.

## Scope

- Add a shared headless workflow using `createHeadlessPlasmonEnvironment()` and the real production Shell taskbar model/commands.
- Start from a pinned-but-not-running native application and prove the expected task entry.
- Launch through the production process path and prove the taskbar transitions to running.
- Focus another window/process and prove active/focused state changes accordingly.
- Minimize and restore/focus through canonical Windowing/Process actions and prove taskbar action/state remains coherent.
- Close the process and prove running state disappears while pin state remains.
- Include one Neutron Element task entry where the headless bridge can truthfully expose running/unknown state without fabricating certainty.
- Avoid assertions on CSS classes when model-level presentation state is the real contract.

## Out of scope

- Implementing #72.
- Alt-Tab (#63).
- Taskbar grouping/cardinality redesign.
- Visual styling or animation acceptance.
- Changing Process/Windowing/Neutron contracts.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A pinned native app transitions through pinned-only -> running -> active/inactive -> minimized/restored -> stopped using production Process/Windowing state.
- [ ] Shell taskbar state reflects those transitions without storing a competing lifecycle authority.
- [ ] Closing a process removes running state while preserving an existing pin.
- [ ] Minimize/focus actions remain consistent with Windowing authority.
- [ ] A representative Element preserves `unknown` semantics without being treated as definitely stopped.
- [ ] The regression uses the shared headless environment and production taskbar seams.
- [ ] No Playwright dependency is added for deterministic lifecycle state.
- [ ] `npm --workspace neutron-plasmon test` passes on the current PR head.
- [ ] Testing/Shell/Process/Windowing documentation remains accurate.

## Verification

Run the focused composed taskbar lifecycle regression plus the full Plasmon fast lane.

## Dependencies / relationships

Blocked by #72 so the regression locks in the accepted coherent taskbar presentation state rather than testing the transitional implementation twice.

## Cross-domain review

- Shell: verify taskbar projection semantics.
- Process / Windowing: verify lifecycle authority is consumed, not redefined.
- Neutron: review only the Element running/unknown assertions.

issues.title: Backfill a headless native document close lifecycle regression across Process and Windowing
issues.body:
## Observation / problem

Process lifecycle and Windowing lifecycle historically had separate focused tests. Issue #41 adds generic close negotiation and #42 wires dirty Text/Markdown document behavior into that seam, but without one cross-authority regression a later change could allow a window-originated close to bypass Process negotiation or allow Process teardown to leave Windowing state inconsistent while each subsystem's isolated tests still pass.

## Expected / desired outcome

Use the shared headless Plasmon environment to prove the accepted native document close lifecycle across production Process, Windowing, and Native Apps seams without relying on browser clicks for deterministic lifecycle semantics.

## Evidence / reproduction

The #30 testing architecture explicitly reserves cross-subsystem semantics for `createHeadlessPlasmonEnvironment()`. #41 establishes the generic Process close-negotiation seam and #42 is the first real dirty-document consumer.

## Context and architecture constraints

- Process owns application lifecycle/close negotiation.
- Windowing owns window geometry/state and close presentation state.
- Native Apps own dirty/save/discard/cancel document semantics.
- Do not move document semantics into Process or Windowing.
- Do not build a test-only process/window implementation.
- Browser tests may still prove the actual close-button adapter if needed, but deterministic allow/prevent/defer/complete/cancel behavior belongs headlessly.

## Scope

- Add one cross-authority headless lifecycle workflow using the #30 environment and real production services/models.
- Open a native document application through the production process/window path.
- Exercise clean close and prove both process and window teardown.
- Exercise dirty close with cancel/prevent and prove the process/window remain coherent.
- Exercise dirty close with save/allow and prove persistence then teardown.
- Exercise discard/allow where supported by #42.
- Exercise deferred close completion and cancellation so repeated close attempts cannot bypass a pending decision.
- Assert no orphaned process/window state after successful close.
- Keep browser-only close-button behavior outside this regression unless a thin adapter assertion is required elsewhere.

## Out of scope

- Implementing #41 or #42.
- Monaco rendering/readiness.
- Broad Native Apps command redesign.
- New Process cardinality semantics.
- Browser-heavy lifecycle scripting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A shared headless workflow proves clean close tears down the corresponding production process/window state.
- [ ] Dirty cancel/prevent leaves the document process/window alive and coherent.
- [ ] Dirty save/allow persists through the production document session before teardown.
- [ ] Discard/allow behavior is covered where supported by the accepted Native Apps seam.
- [ ] Deferred close cannot be bypassed by repeated ordinary close requests.
- [ ] Successful completion leaves no orphaned process or window record.
- [ ] The regression uses `createHeadlessPlasmonEnvironment()` and production seams rather than duplicate fakes.
- [ ] No Playwright dependency is added for deterministic lifecycle semantics.
- [ ] `npm --workspace neutron-plasmon test` passes on the current PR head.
- [ ] Testing/Process/Windowing/Native Apps documentation remains accurate.

## Verification

Run the focused lifecycle regression plus the full Plasmon fast lane.

## Dependencies / relationships

Blocked by #41 and #42 so the regression locks in the accepted generic close seam and its first real dirty-document consumer.

## Cross-domain review

- Process: verify lifecycle assertions respect Process authority.
- Windowing: verify close/state assertions do not move policy upward.
- Native Apps: verify dirty/save/discard semantics are consumed rather than redefined.

issues.title: Replace raw taskbar runtime flags with coherent pinned/running/active/launching presentation state
issues.body:
## Observation / problem

The current Shell taskbar mixes several different concepts directly in rendering. Native entries infer `running` from process presence and `active` from the current taskbar action, while Neutron Element entries expose the raw runtime string `yes` / `no` / `unknown` directly in the UI as `<small>{entry.running}</small>`. Shell also tracks transient `busyId` during actions, but that launching/busy state is not represented coherently in the taskbar model.

This produces implementation-oriented presentation instead of a clear desktop task state.

## Expected / desired outcome

Define a small Shell taskbar presentation state that cleanly distinguishes pinned, running, active/focused, and launching/transitioning state for native apps and Neutron Elements without redefining Process or Neutron runtime authority.

## Evidence / reproduction

`deriveTaskbarEntries()` currently exposes `pinned`, native `process`, and Element `running`. `Shell.tsx` then derives classes ad hoc and renders Neutron's raw runtime state text `yes` / `no` / `unknown` directly on the taskbar button. `busyId` is tracked separately for asynchronous Shell actions rather than being part of a coherent taskbar presentation model.

## Context and architecture constraints

- Process remains authoritative for native process lifecycle.
- Windowing remains authoritative for native focus/minimize state.
- NeutronBridge remains authoritative for Element runtime observations.
- Shell owns the user-facing taskbar projection of those authorities.
- Do not invent a shadow runtime state or reinterpret `unknown` as definitely stopped.
- Keep deterministic state derivation below React.

## Scope

- Introduce a focused taskbar presentation-state derivation for native and Element entries.
- Distinguish at least pinned-only, launching/busy, running, and active/focused where the underlying authorities can truthfully establish those states.
- Preserve uncertainty when Neutron runtime state is unknown without displaying raw implementation tokens to the user.
- Make taskbar buttons consume the derived presentation state rather than ad hoc React conditionals.
- Preserve existing launch/focus/minimize actions.
- Add focused model tests for pinned/running/focused/unknown/launching transitions.
- Update taskbar accessibility labels to describe user-facing state.

## Out of scope

- Changing Neutron runtime-state contracts.
- Process lifecycle redesign.
- Alt-Tab (#63).
- Taskbar grouping/cardinality redesign.
- Broad taskbar visual redesign.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Taskbar UI no longer renders raw Neutron `yes` / `no` / `unknown` tokens as user-facing status text.
- [ ] Native and Element task entries derive coherent user-facing pinned/running/active/launching presentation state from canonical authorities.
- [ ] `unknown` Neutron state remains explicitly uncertain and is not treated as a confirmed stopped state.
- [ ] Launching/busy state is represented without creating a second runtime authority.
- [ ] Existing native launch/focus/minimize behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] Focused model tests cover representative state transitions.
- [ ] `npm --workspace neutron-plasmon test` passes on the current PR head.
- [ ] Shell README/AGENTS remain accurate.

## Verification

Use deterministic Shell model tests for presentation-state derivation plus a small packaged/manual check for visible taskbar status and accessibility labels.

## Dependencies / relationships

Independent Shell convergence work. It can follow #32/#61 if those changes overlap the same Shell component, but it does not require a new runtime contract.

## Cross-domain review

- Process/Windowing: verify native lifecycle/focus authority is only consumed.
- Neutron: verify Element `unknown` semantics are preserved rather than reinterpreted.

issues.title: Add packaged Monaco acceptance for Text and Markdown editors
issues.body:
## Observation / problem

Text and Markdown both depend on the real packaged Monaco/browser boundary, but current fast tests primarily prove document/session and adapter configuration. Issue #33 establishes a small packaged Playwright lane and currently proves packaged asset/worker serving, not the full native editor workflow itself.

A regression can therefore leave Monaco assets technically present while Text or Markdown fails to create a usable editor, receive focus, edit content, save, or reopen in the actual packaged Plasmon environment.

## Expected / desired outcome

Add a small Native Apps-owned packaged acceptance journey proving the real Text and Markdown Monaco surfaces initialize and complete their core open/edit/save/reopen workflows through normal Plasmon production paths.

## Evidence / reproduction

`native-apps/text` contains `MonacoEditorSurface.tsx`, Monaco environment/adapter code, and fast adapter/document tests. The Text README explicitly states that Monaco creation/readiness, workers/assets, focus/selection, keyboard commands, and rendered editor behavior require real-browser/package testing. Markdown is a separate first-class native app and shares the editor/document infrastructure.

## Context and architecture constraints

- Feature owners own regression coverage for their application behavior; Testing owns shared Playwright infrastructure.
- Reuse #33's packaged lane rather than creating a second browser harness.
- Keep document/save/conflict semantics covered headlessly; browser tests should prove only the real Monaco/package interaction boundary.
- Open files through the normal association/open/process/window path where practical rather than mounting editor components directly as a substitute for application acceptance.
- Do not turn this into exhaustive editor UI automation.

## Scope

- Add one compact packaged Text journey and one compact packaged Markdown journey.
- Prove Monaco becomes genuinely ready/interactive, not merely that worker URLs return 200.
- Open a filesystem-backed document through the normal product path.
- Edit content through the real Monaco surface.
- Save through the production application command/session path.
- Close/reopen and verify persisted content.
- Include a stable readiness/semantic selector contract suitable for future editor regressions.
- Reuse shared setup between Text and Markdown where the product architecture already shares behavior.

## Out of scope

- Re-testing all deterministic document-session semantics in Playwright.
- Broad keyboard-command matrix.
- Pixel/screenshot regression.
- Dirty-close confirmation (#42).
- Monaco package/version upgrades.
- Generic browser automation framework changes beyond a concrete missing #33 helper.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Packaged Text can open a real filesystem document and reach a usable Monaco editor state.
- [x] Packaged Markdown can open a real filesystem document and reach a usable Monaco editor state.
- [x] Each journey edits and saves through the production application path.
- [x] Reopen proves saved content came from filesystem persistence rather than test-only component state.
- [x] The browser tests use stable semantic/readiness signals and do not duplicate broad deterministic document tests.
- [x] Monaco worker/asset failures produce an actionable failing acceptance test.
- [x] Relevant focused/fast tests remain green.
- [x] Native Apps/Text/Markdown testing documentation remains accurate.

## Verification

Run through the packaged Playwright lane established by #33 plus the normal Plasmon fast suite.

## Dependencies / relationships

Blocked by #33 — reuse the accepted packaged Playwright infrastructure rather than introducing another harness.

Related to #42 but independent of dirty-close semantics.

## Cross-domain review

- Testing: verify the new journeys remain small and browser-boundary focused.

issues.title: Render Desktop/FileManager drag previews above the window stack
issues.body:
## Observation / problem

Current FileManager drag interaction visually moves the actual selected entry DOM elements with `translate3d(...)`. In Desktop presentation those source entries live in the desktop/FileManager layer, so the drag representation remains constrained to that stacking context and can pass visually underneath application windows while the user drags across the desktop.

## Expected / desired outcome

Desktop/FileManager resource drags should present a clear top-level drag preview that remains visible above normal windows while preserving the existing production drag/drop semantics and selected-resource identity.

## Evidence / reproduction

`FileManager.tsx` currently applies transforms directly to each active entry in `applyDragTransform()` and removes them in `clearDragVisual()`. There is no detached/top-level drag-preview layer for the active drag gesture.

## Context and architecture constraints

- FileManager owns selection and drag/drop resource semantics.
- Windowing owns window z-order; this Issue should not mutate window focus/z just to make a drag visible.
- The drag preview is presentation only and must not become a second drag/drop state machine.
- Preserve multi-selection drag behavior and canonical directory-drop targeting.
- Use browser/portal layering only where needed to escape the Desktop stacking context.

## Scope

- Introduce a presentation-only drag preview for active resource drags.
- Render it in a layer above normal application windows without changing window z-order.
- Represent multi-selection clearly without cloning every full resource surface unnecessarily.
- Keep pointer/drop hit-testing against actual canonical targets rather than against the preview.
- Preserve Desktop free-position dragging and directory drop semantics.
- Ensure cleanup on pointer release/cancel/unmount.
- Add deterministic helper tests where applicable plus a browser-level interaction test for stacking/hit-testing.

## Out of scope

- Redesigning drag selection thresholds.
- Changing filesystem move/copy semantics.
- Window focus/z-order changes.
- Cross-browser native HTML5 drag-and-drop replacement.
- Broad visual restyle of FileManager entries.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] An active Desktop/FileManager resource drag remains visibly represented above normal native windows.
- [x] The preview does not intercept or corrupt canonical drop-target hit-testing.
- [x] Multi-selected resources retain the existing group-drag semantics.
- [x] Desktop reposition and directory-drop outcomes are unchanged except for the improved presentation.
- [x] Pointer cancel/release/unmount reliably removes the preview.
- [x] Browser-level coverage proves the preview stacks above a normal native window while the underlying drop behavior still works.
- [x] `npm --workspace neutron-plasmon test` passes on the current PR head.
- [x] FileManager/Desktop/Visual documentation remains accurate.

## Verification

Use focused drag/helper tests for deterministic state and a real browser test for portal/stacking/hit-testing because that boundary depends on DOM layering.

## Dependencies / relationships

Independent visual/interaction correction. It should not be combined with #65 operation progress or #43 window snapping.

## Cross-domain review

- Windowing: verify no window focus/z-order authority is moved into FileManager.
- Visual: review only if a shared overlay primitive is added.

issues.title: Add visible progress state for long-running FileManager import and paste operations
issues.body:
## Observation / problem

Current FileManager import and paste operations are awaited as opaque asynchronous actions. Multi-file import loops through files sequentially and reports only final failures; paste likewise waits for completion without exposing in-progress state. For large resources, users cannot tell whether Plasmon is actively copying/importing, stalled, or safe to interact with again.

## Expected / desired outcome

Expose deterministic FileManager operation state for long-running import and paste workflows so the UI can show meaningful progress/busy status without moving filesystem semantics into React.

## Evidence / reproduction

`FileManager.tsx` currently:

- loops `for (const file of files)` and awaits `importFileIntoFs()` for each item;
- awaits `pasteClipboardCollisionAware()` as one opaque operation;
- maintains general loading/error state but no file-operation progress snapshot.

## Context and architecture constraints

- Filesystem owns actual copy/move/write semantics.
- FileManager owns user-facing operation orchestration and presentation.
- Deterministic operation state should live below React where practical and be testable without DOM timing.
- Do not create a generic background-job framework solely for this Issue.
- Do not fake byte progress when the underlying filesystem operation cannot actually report it; item-level progress is acceptable where that is the truthful boundary.

## Scope

- Add a small production operation-state model for import/paste workflows.
- Represent operation kind, running/completed/failed state, item counts, and current item where reliably known.
- Prevent accidental duplicate execution of the same destructive/expensive action while its operation is already active where appropriate.
- Surface partial multi-file import failures without hiding successful items.
- Preserve existing collision and filesystem semantics.
- Add focused headless/model tests.
- Add the minimal UI needed to expose current progress/status accessibly.

## Out of scope

- Generic system-wide job manager.
- Byte-accurate progress when FsService does not expose byte progress.
- Cancellation unless the underlying production operation already supports safe cancellation.
- Trash/Delete redesign (#40).
- Drag visual redesign.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Import exposes truthful operation progress/state while multiple files are processed.
- [ ] Paste exposes running/completed/failed state rather than appearing inert during long operations.
- [ ] Partial import success/failure remains deterministic and visible.
- [ ] React renders production operation state rather than implementing a second state machine.
- [ ] Unsupported byte-level progress is not fabricated.
- [ ] Focused headless/model tests cover success, partial failure, and duplicate-trigger protection where applicable.
- [ ] `npm --workspace neutron-plasmon test` passes on the current PR head.
- [ ] FileManager README/AGENTS remain accurate.

## Verification

Use deterministic model tests for operation transitions and a small packaged/manual/browser check for visible progress during a deliberately non-trivial import/paste workload.

## Dependencies / relationships

Independent FileManager UX/correctness improvement. It should not be combined with #31, #40, #44, or #51.

## Cross-domain review

- Filesystem only if progress requires changing an FsService contract rather than consuming existing boundaries.

issues.title: Persist js-dos game progress across close and reopen through Plasmon filesystem state
issues.body:
## Observation / problem

The current js-dos player explicitly starts the runtime with `autoSave: false` and tears the player down on window close. There is no Plasmon-owned save-state persistence path tied to the selected filesystem game resource, so reopening a game cannot currently rely on durable progress through the Plasmon filesystem authority.

## Expected / desired outcome

Integrate the supported js-dos save-state/export lifecycle with Plasmon filesystem-backed durable state so progress for a game resource can survive process/window close and reopen without creating a browser-local shadow source of truth.

## Evidence / reproduction

`JsDosPlayer.tsx` reads the selected `.jsdos` resource from FsService, constructs the browser runtime, configures `autoSave: false`, and calls `player.stop()` during teardown. The runtime host README currently documents runtime loading/browser behavior but no durable save-state ownership contract.

## Context and architecture constraints

- The selected game resource remains filesystem-owned.
- Durable game progress promised by Plasmon must be persisted through the Plasmon filesystem/service authority, not silently through localStorage/IndexedDB/runtime-private durable state.
- js-dos owns genuine engine-specific save/export/import mechanics.
- Do not mutate the original game bundle merely to store progress unless the runtime format explicitly requires and the UX contract chooses that behavior.
- Prefer stable NodeId association between a game resource and its save/progress data.
- Do not introduce game-title-specific paths or logic.

## Scope

- Audit the packaged js-dos version/API for supported save/export/import mechanics.
- Define a filesystem-backed save-state representation tied to the stable identity of the opened game resource.
- Capture supported progress at explicit save/teardown boundaries without blocking close indefinitely.
- Restore the latest compatible saved progress when reopening the same game resource.
- Handle missing/corrupt/incompatible save data with a deterministic fallback to normal startup and a useful error/warning boundary.
- Ensure deleting/moving/renaming the game does not accidentally associate progress by mutable basename alone.
- Add focused persistence/lifecycle tests plus packaged/browser proof using a legal/test bundle where state change can be observed.
- Update js-dos/Games documentation with the durable save ownership contract.

## Out of scope

- Cloud synchronization beyond normal Plasmon filesystem durability.
- Cross-device conflict resolution.
- Generic emulator save-state framework before EmulatorJS (#48) establishes a second real runtime.
- Save-state screenshots/artwork.
- Game library/catalog UI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The supported js-dos save/export/import capability is established from the actual packaged runtime/API.
- [x] Durable progress is stored through Plasmon filesystem authority rather than a browser-local durable shadow store.
- [x] Save identity is tied to stable game-resource identity rather than basename/path alone where NodeId is available.
- [x] Closing and reopening a game can restore previously persisted progress in a real packaged/browser run.
- [x] Rename/move of the game resource does not orphan progress solely because the visible path changed.
- [x] Missing/corrupt/incompatible save data fails safely and does not prevent launching the original game.
- [x] Focused persistence/lifecycle tests pass.
- [x] Relevant packaged/browser acceptance passes.
- [x] `npm --workspace neutron-plasmon test` passes on the current PR head.
- [x] Games/js-dos README/AGENTS remain accurate.

## Verification

Use deterministic persistence mapping/lifecycle tests first. Final acceptance requires a real browser/package run proving progress changes, close, reopen, and restore.

## Dependencies / relationships

Independent of #48. If #48 later exposes a genuinely shared save lifecycle, extract common behavior only from proven duplication rather than pre-designing a generic emulator framework.

## Cross-domain review

- Filesystem: verify durable state uses canonical filesystem identity/persistence.
- Testing: review packaged proof if reusable browser helpers are added.

issues.title: Add an Alt-Tab window switcher that consumes Windowing focus history
issues.body:
## Observation / problem

Plasmon currently has pointer/taskbar-driven focus but no canonical keyboard window switcher. Once Windowing exposes deterministic MRU focus history, Shell can provide the familiar Alt-Tab interaction without inventing a separate focus ordering policy.

## Expected / desired outcome

Add a Shell-owned Alt-Tab presentation/keyboard interaction that enumerates switchable native windows from the Windowing MRU seam and commits selection through the existing WindowManager focus authority.

## Evidence / reproduction

Current Windowing has no Alt-Tab consumer and Shell does not expose a keyboard switcher. #62 establishes the prerequisite deterministic focus-history contract below Shell.

## Context and architecture constraints

- Windowing owns focus history and final focus/minimize/restore behavior.
- Shell owns global keyboard interaction and switcher presentation.
- Do not derive a competing MRU order from process arrays, DOM order, taskbar order, or raw z values.
- Keep keyboard state deterministic below React where practical.
- Preserve normal browser/system shortcuts where Plasmon does not own the event.

## Scope

- Handle the supported Alt-Tab keyboard sequence at the Shell/browser boundary.
- Build switcher entries from Windowing's accepted MRU/focus-history seam.
- Support cycling while Alt remains held and committing the selected window when the gesture completes.
- Restore/focus minimized windows through normal WindowManager focus behavior.
- Exclude closed/non-switchable entries deterministically.
- Provide accessible labels/icons using existing process/window/application presentation data.
- Add focused Shell model/controller tests plus a small browser test for the real keyboard event boundary.

## Out of scope

- Defining Windowing MRU semantics (#62).
- Virtual desktops/workspaces.
- Mission Control/Task View overview UI.
- Reworking taskbar grouping.
- Custom global hotkeys unrelated to window switching.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Alt-Tab cycles through the canonical Windowing MRU order rather than a Shell-local substitute.
- [x] The selected window is focused through WindowManager authority.
- [x] Minimized selected windows are restored/focused consistently with existing focus semantics.
- [x] Closed/non-switchable windows do not remain in the visible cycle.
- [x] Keyboard cycling/commit/cancel behavior is deterministic and covered below React where practical.
- [x] A browser-level test proves the actual keyboard adapter reaches the production switcher behavior.
- [x] `npm --workspace neutron-plasmon test` passes on the current PR head.
- [x] Shell/Windowing documentation remains accurate.

## Verification

Use Shell/controller tests for switching semantics and a small packaged/browser check for the actual Alt-Tab event boundary.

## Dependencies / relationships

Blocked by #62 — Windowing must first expose the accepted deterministic focus-history seam.

## Cross-domain review

- Windowing: verify Shell consumes rather than redefines focus authority.
- Visual: review only if shared presentation primitives change.

issues.title: Add Send to Desktop shortcut command for eligible resources
issues.body:
## Observation / problem

Plasmon already has a canonical filesystem shortcut format and `createShortcut()` helper that can create stable NodeId-backed shortcuts, but FileManager does not currently expose the familiar `Send to Desktop` convenience action for selected filesystem resources.

Users therefore have the underlying shortcut capability without a direct desktop-oriented command.

## Expected / desired outcome

FileManager can create a shortcut to an eligible selected resource directly on `/Desktop` using the canonical shortcut primitive and stable target identity.

## Evidence / reproduction

`apps/plasmon/src/os/fs/shortcut.ts` already provides `createShortcut(fs, parentId, target, options)` and collision-safe naming. FileManager currently exposes create/import/copy/cut/paste/delete/properties/open-with style actions but no Send to Desktop shortcut command.

## Context and architecture constraints

- Filesystem owns shortcut serialization and stable target identity.
- FileManager owns command presentation/selection only.
- Node targets must use stable NodeId rather than mutable visible paths.
- Do not create a separate desktop-link format or duplicate shortcut naming logic.
- This is a convenience command, not a generic command-framework refactor.

## Scope

- Add `Send to Desktop` / `Desktop (create shortcut)` for eligible selected resources.
- Resolve the canonical `/Desktop` directory through FsService.
- Create the shortcut using the shared filesystem `createShortcut()` primitive.
- Preserve canonical collision-safe naming.
- Surface useful errors if Desktop is unavailable or the selected resource is not eligible.
- Add focused production-model/FileManager tests.

## Out of scope

- Moving/copying the original resource to Desktop.
- External Windows `.lnk` compatibility.
- Shortcut-opening semantics (#31).
- Shortcut visual overlay/presentation work.
- Generic shell context-menu framework redesign.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An eligible selected filesystem resource can be sent to Desktop as a shortcut.
- [ ] The shortcut target uses canonical stable NodeId identity for filesystem resources.
- [ ] Shortcut serialization/naming is delegated to the existing filesystem shortcut primitive.
- [ ] Existing destination-name collisions are handled by canonical unique-name behavior.
- [ ] The original resource is not moved or copied.
- [ ] Error behavior is deterministic when `/Desktop` or the target is unavailable.
- [ ] Focused tests cover successful creation, collision naming, and failure boundaries.
- [ ] `npm --workspace neutron-plasmon test` passes on the current PR head.
- [ ] Applicable FileManager/filesystem README/AGENTS remain accurate.

## Verification

Use headless/model tests to prove destination and stable target identity. Packaged/manual validation can later confirm discoverability in the visible FileManager context menu.

## Dependencies / relationships

Related to #44 Create Shortcut, but this Issue can consume the already-existing filesystem shortcut primitive independently.

## Cross-domain review

- Filesystem: verify canonical shortcut creation and Desktop identity are consumed without duplication.

issues.title: Add EmulatorJS as a second association-driven game runtime
issues.body:
## Observation / problem

Plasmon currently has js-dos as a real association-driven local game/runtime integration, but no EmulatorJS runtime is present in the active native-app/runtime tree. The Games direction explicitly calls for game resources to participate in the same filesystem/opening model rather than gaining title-specific launch logic.

A second real runtime is the appropriate next step before extracting any generic emulator/runtime abstraction.

## Expected / desired outcome

Add EmulatorJS as a normal runtime selected through file associations and launched through the existing process/window/opening authorities, with packaged browser proof for one representative supported ROM/bundle path.

## Evidence / reproduction

Current source contains `native-apps/jsdos/**` and js-dos registration, but no EmulatorJS implementation. Current Games documentation says reusable runtimes belong under the native-app/runtime boundary and should be association-driven.

## Context and architecture constraints

- Do not create a separate Games launcher or title-specific opening path.
- Filesystem remains authoritative for user game resources and saves.
- Runtime selection belongs to AssociationRegistry/OpenService.
- Process/Windowing own native host lifecycle.
- Treat this as the second concrete runtime; only after two real runtimes exist should shared lifecycle extraction be considered.
- Do not copy js-dos implementation details blindly where EmulatorJS has different lifecycle/assets/security needs.

## Scope

- Add an EmulatorJS runtime under the appropriate native-app/runtime boundary.
- Register supported extensions/MIME/resource types through AssociationRegistry.
- Launch through the existing OpenService/process/window path.
- Load runtime assets through package-safe paths appropriate to Plasmon/Neutron packaging.
- Support one explicit representative game/ROM workflow for acceptance without seeding title-specific behavior into Shell/FileManager.
- Handle runtime loading/error/teardown deterministically.
- Keep save/persistence integration filesystem-backed where the selected EmulatorJS integration exposes save data.
- Add focused association/runtime tests and packaged/browser proof of actual runtime initialization.

## Out of scope

- Generic emulator framework extraction.
- Broad game library/catalog UI.
- Bundling unlicensed commercial ROMs.
- js-dos redesign.
- Perfect controller/fullscreen/audio UX beyond what is required for the first supported EmulatorJS path.

issues.title: Add a native Recycle Bin surface for restore, permanent delete, and empty
issues.body:
## Observation / problem

Plasmon has canonical filesystem Trash semantics under `/System/.Trash`, including restore and permanent-delete behavior, but lacks a first-class user-facing Recycle Bin/Trash application surface integrated through the native process/window stack.

Without that surface, users cannot inspect trashed items, restore them, permanently delete selected entries, or empty Trash through the normal OS UI.

## Expected / desired outcome

Add a real Plasmon-native Recycle Bin application that projects the canonical filesystem Trash authority without duplicating Trash storage/schema semantics.

## Scope

- Register a native Recycle Bin application through the shared native application registry/process stack.
- Reconcile its system application entry through the existing filesystem/bootstrap authority.
- Render canonical Trash entries through `TrashService`/filesystem APIs, not direct `.Trash` parsing.
- Support Restore using canonical restore semantics, including collision/fallback behavior and stable NodeId preservation.
- Support explicit permanent delete for selected entries with confirmation.
- Support explicit Empty Recycle Bin with confirmation.
- Refresh when relevant filesystem/Trash state changes externally.
- Add focused model/integration tests plus a packaged/browser proof that the native surface launches and renders.
- Keep the application presentation within Native Apps; keep Trash semantics in Filesystem.

## Out of scope

- Redesigning Trash storage/schema.
- New filesystem delete semantics.
- Shell/Desktop trash shortcuts beyond what normal system-app projection already provides.
- Visual redesign outside the new native app surface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Recycle Bin exists as a real first-class native application/system surface.
- [x] The application lists/displays entries from canonical Trash authority rather than a shadow store.
- [x] Restore delegates to `TrashService` semantics, including fallback/collision behavior and NodeId preservation.
- [x] Permanent delete is explicit and confirmation-gated.
- [x] Empty Recycle Bin is explicit and confirmation-gated.
- [x] External filesystem/Trash mutation invalidates and refreshes the application view.
- [x] The app does not duplicate Trash wrapper/schema logic or directly mutate/parse `/System/.Trash` storage.
- [x] Native app registration/bootstrap/system-app projection is correct.
- [x] Focused fast tests cover native registration, list/restore, permanent delete, empty, and external invalidation.
- [x] `npm --workspace neutron-plasmon test` passes on the current PR head.
- [x] Packaged/browser validation proves the native Recycle Bin surface launches and renders through the real Shell/process/window path.
- [x] Native Apps/Filesystem documentation remains accurate.

## Verification

Use deterministic model/integration coverage for Trash operations and a small packaged browser proof for the native application launch/render boundary.

## Dependencies / relationships

Uses existing filesystem Trash authority; does not change that authority.

## Cross-domain review

- Filesystem: verify the native app remains a consumer of canonical Trash semantics and does not duplicate filesystem policy.

issues.title: Expose Create Shortcut in FileManager using the canonical shortcut primitive
issues.body:
## Observation / problem

The filesystem layer already provides `createShortcut()` and the versioned `plasmon.shortcut` metadata format for native applications, Neutron Elements, filesystem nodes, and URLs. FileManager currently exposes create folder/document/import actions but does not expose a user-facing Create Shortcut command for selected filesystem resources.

## Expected / desired outcome

Users can create a normal filesystem shortcut from FileManager without FileManager inventing its own shortcut format or path-based identity model.

## Evidence / reproduction

`apps/plasmon/src/os/fs/shortcut.ts` provides `createShortcut(fs, parentId, target, options)` plus collision-safe naming and stable NodeId targets. Current `FileManager.tsx` does not consume that primitive for a Create Shortcut action.

## Context and architecture constraints

- Filesystem owns shortcut persistence/metadata and stable target identity.
- Node-target shortcuts should prefer NodeId rather than mutable visible paths.
- FileManager owns command presentation/selection, not shortcut serialization.
- Do not create `.lnk` compatibility or a second shortcut format in this Issue.

## Scope

- Add a FileManager command for creating a shortcut to an eligible selected resource.
- Use the canonical filesystem `createShortcut()` behavior.
- Place the created shortcut in the current directory with collision-safe naming.
- Keep the new shortcut selected and available for normal rename behavior after creation where practical.
- Respect canonical resource capabilities/policy when deciding whether the command is available.
- Add focused production-model/FileManager tests.

## Out of scope

- Send to Desktop convenience command.
- Shortcut icon-overlay redesign.
- Shortcut opening semantics (#31).
- External Windows `.lnk` import/export.
- Generic command-framework redesign.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] FileManager exposes Create Shortcut for eligible selected resources.
- [ ] Created filesystem-resource shortcuts use stable NodeId targets through the canonical shortcut metadata format.
- [ ] Naming collisions are handled by the existing canonical unique-name semantics.
- [ ] FileManager does not duplicate shortcut serialization or target-resolution logic.
- [ ] The created shortcut participates in normal selection/rename behavior.
- [ ] Focused tests cover creation and collision behavior through the user-facing production command seam.
- [ ] `npm --workspace neutron-plasmon test` passes on the current PR head.
- [ ] Applicable README/AGENTS remain accurate.

## Verification

Use focused headless/model tests for creation and metadata identity. Packaged/manual verification can later confirm context-menu/keyboard discoverability and visible interaction.

## Dependencies / relationships

Independent of #31 implementation, though #31 is required for the resulting shortcut to open through the canonical dispatcher from FileManager.

## Cross-domain review

- Filesystem: verify the existing shortcut primitive is consumed without redefining shortcut authority.

issues.title: Add deterministic left/right edge snapping to native windows
issues.body:
## Observation / problem

Plasmon's native window manager already owns deterministic geometry, maximize/restore, viewport constraints, focus, minimize, and drag/resize commits. It does not currently expose a snap state or edge-snap geometry for arranging a window to a half-screen region, leaving a common desktop window-management interaction unavailable.

## Expected / desired outcome

Add a bounded, testable left/right edge-snapping behavior that fits the existing window-state/geometry authority and keeps browser pointer detection as a thin adapter.

## Evidence / reproduction

`NativeWindowManager` currently models normal, minimized, and maximized states plus restore geometry. `geometry.ts` owns pure viewport/window calculations. There is no current snap mode/geometry in the manager contract.

## Context and architecture constraints

- Windowing owns floating-window geometry/state; Shell must not own snap geometry.
- Keep snap state transitions deterministic below React.
- Browser drag-edge detection may live in the thin window interaction adapter, but final state/geometry must be committed through the window manager.
- Preserve restore geometry so dragging/restoring a snapped window does not lose its prior usable geometry.
- Do not turn this into a tiling-window-manager framework.

## Scope

- Add left-half and right-half snap geometry/state for the current viewport.
- Provide deterministic manager operations/state transitions for entering/exiting snap.
- Preserve an appropriate pre-snap restore geometry.
- Recompute snapped geometry when the available viewport changes.
- Integrate drag-to-left/right-edge detection through the existing browser interaction layer.
- Ensure maximize/minimize/restore/focus behavior remains coherent when a window is snapped.
- Add pure geometry/manager tests and small browser interaction coverage where edge detection itself requires DOM/pointer behavior.

## Out of scope

- Quarter/corner layouts.
- Multi-monitor layout management.
- Fancy snap-layout chooser UI.
- Shell-owned tiling policy.
- Persisted placement across sessions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A native window can enter a deterministic left-half snap state.
- [x] A native window can enter a deterministic right-half snap state.
- [x] Snapped geometry is derived from the manager's available viewport and respects its coordinate origin.
- [x] Exiting snap restores a sensible pre-snap geometry rather than leaving the half-screen rectangle as the normal placement.
- [x] Minimize, focus, maximize and restore transitions do not corrupt snap/restore state.
- [x] Viewport changes recompute snapped geometry consistently.
- [x] Pure geometry/manager tests cover snap transitions and viewport changes.
- [x] Browser-level coverage verifies the drag-edge adapter where practical.
- [x] `npm --workspace neutron-plasmon test` passes on the current PR head.
- [x] Windowing README/AGENTS and public contracts remain accurate.

## Verification

Use deterministic geometry/manager tests for state correctness and a browser interaction test for pointer-edge activation. Manual validation remains useful for drag feel but is not a substitute for manager tests.

## Dependencies / relationships

Independent Windowing feature. It should not block the current open-dispatch/test-harness convergence work.

## Cross-domain review

- Process only if lifecycle/focus semantics outside the existing WindowManager contract must change.
